quotes.quote: Am I my brother's keeper?
quotes.context: Asked after murdering his brother in a field.

quotes.quote: Here am I; send me.
quotes.context: Volunteering after a live coal touched his lips in the temple.

quotes.quote: Whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.
quotes.context: Refusing to leave her mother-in-law on the road out of Moab.

quotes.quote: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him.
quotes.context: Spoken after losing his children, his wealth and his health.

quotes.quote: I know that my redeemer liveth.
quotes.context: Spoken from an ash heap while his friends accused him.

quotes.quote: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.
quotes.context: Answering an angel who announced an impossible pregnancy.

quotes.quote: What is truth?
quotes.context: Asked by a Roman governor during a trial he wanted no part of.

quotes.quote: Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.
quotes.context: Answering at Caesarea Philippi when the others stayed quiet.

quotes.quote: Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, I will not believe.
quotes.context: Spoken to the other disciples a week after the resurrection.

quotes.quote: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge.
quotes.context: Prayed for his own killers while the stones were still falling.

quotes.quote: Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee.
quotes.context: Said to a lame beggar at the Beautiful gate of the temple.

quotes.quote: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.
quotes.context: Written from prison to a younger minister near the end of his life.

quotes.quote: He must increase, but I must decrease.
quotes.context: Said when his own disciples complained that crowds were leaving him.

quotes.quote: Let my people go.
quotes.context: Delivered repeatedly to a stubborn king of Egypt.

quotes.quote: Choose you this day whom ye will serve... but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
quotes.context: A farewell challenge to Israel at Shechem.

quotes.quote: Speak; for thy servant heareth.
quotes.context: Said by a boy who had mistaken God's voice for the old priest's.

quotes.quote: Is there not a cause?
quotes.context: Said to an older brother who mocked him for coming to the battle line.

quotes.quote: Thou art the man.
quotes.context: A prophet's verdict after telling a king a story about a stolen lamb.

quotes.quote: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people.
quotes.context: Asked at Gibeon when God offered him anything he wanted.

quotes.quote: How long halt ye between two opinions? If the Lord be God, follow him.
quotes.context: Shouted to Israel on Mount Carmel before the fire fell.

quotes.quote: I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.
quotes.context: Asked of his master just before a whirlwind took him away.

quotes.quote: If I perish, I perish.
quotes.context: Decided before going to the king unbidden to save her people.

quotes.quote: Who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
quotes.context: Sent as a message to a queen who was hesitating.

quotes.quote: I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down.
quotes.context: Refusing a meeting with enemies while rebuilding a wall.

quotes.quote: Our God whom we serve is able to deliver us... but if not, we will not serve thy gods.
quotes.context: Said to a king standing in front of a very hot furnace.

quotes.quote: Ah, Lord God! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child.
quotes.context: Protesting his own call as a prophet to the nations.

quotes.quote: I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.
quotes.context: Complaining to God about a nation that would not stop murmuring.

quotes.quote: Nay; but we will have a king over us.
quotes.context: Demanded of an aging judge, so they could be like other nations.

quotes.quote: The Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.
quotes.context: Said on the same day he lost everything he owned and all his children.

quotes.quote: Create in me a clean heart, O God.
quotes.context: Written after a prophet confronted him about Bathsheba.

quotes.quote: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.
quotes.context: Said while pointing out a man walking toward him at the Jordan.

quotes.quote: Master, carest thou not that we perish?
quotes.context: Shouted in a storm at someone who was asleep on a pillow.

quotes.quote: Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
quotes.context: Said by a grieving sister four days after the funeral in Bethany.

quotes.quote: What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ?
quotes.context: Asked of a crowd that had just chosen Barabbas.

quotes.quote: Truly this man was the Son of God.
quotes.context: Said by a Roman soldier watching the crucifixion end.

quotes.quote: My Lord and my God.
quotes.context: Cried out by the doubter once he finally saw the wounds.

quotes.quote: Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?
quotes.context: Asked from the ground on the road to Damascus, blinded by light.

quotes.quote: Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
quotes.context: Said by a king after hearing a prisoner's defense.

quotes.quote: Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.
quotes.context: Rebuking a former sorcerer who offered cash for the Holy Ghost.

quotes.quote: Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
quotes.context: Asked after an earthquake opened every cell door at midnight.

quotes.quote: Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?
quotes.context: A skeptical first reaction to news of the Messiah.

quotes.quote: Entreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee.
quotes.context: Clinging to a bitter widow who told her to go home.

quotes.quote: Call me not Pleasant, call me Bitter: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.
quotes.context: Said on returning to Bethlehem empty after years in Moab.

quotes.quote: Give me children, or else I die.
quotes.context: Demanded of her husband while envying her own sister.

quotes.quote: I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.
quotes.context: Said during an all-night wrestling match by the brook Jabbok.

quotes.quote: Ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.
quotes.context: Said to the brothers who had sold him into slavery.

quotes.quote: How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
quotes.context: Refusing his master's wife in Egypt.

quotes.quote: Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?
quotes.context: Bargaining with God over the fate of Sodom.

quotes.quote: Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?
quotes.context: Asked of his father on the way up Mount Moriah.

quotes.quote: Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing.
quotes.context: Explained to a son who returned from hunting too late.

quotes.quote: What hast thou done unto me? I took thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast blessed them.
quotes.context: An angry Moabite king complaining to the prophet he had hired.

quotes.quote: What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?
quotes.context: Spoken by an animal that could see what its rider could not.

quotes.quote: Is it well with thee? is it well with thy husband? is it well with the child? And she answered, It is well.
quotes.context: Said by a mother riding for help, her dead son left on a prophet's bed.

quotes.quote: Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.
quotes.context: Reassuring a terrified servant surrounded by an enemy army.

quotes.quote: If I had not plowed with my heifer, ye had not found out my riddle.
quotes.context: Said after his wedding guests pressured his bride for the answer.

quotes.quote: O Lord God, remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once.
quotes.context: Prayed blind, between two pillars, in a Philistine temple.

quotes.quote: If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.
quotes.context: Said to a prophetess who had just given him his marching orders.

quotes.quote: For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition.
quotes.context: Said while handing her young son over to the priest at Shiloh.

quotes.quote: I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord... because I feared the people.
quotes.context: Confessed to Samuel after sparing the Amalekite livestock.

quotes.quote: Thy people shall be my people... the Lord do so to me, and more also, if ought but death part thee and me.
quotes.context: The full form of a vow made on the road out of Moab.

quotes.quote: Arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.
quotes.context: Said to a sleeping passenger during a storm bound for Tarshish.

quotes.quote: I do well to be angry, even unto death.
quotes.context: Sulking outside a city that had just repented, over a withered plant.

quotes.quote: How shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife well stricken in years.
quotes.context: Doubting an angel at the altar of incense, and struck dumb for it.

quotes.quote: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.
quotes.context: Instructions to servants at a wedding in Cana that ran out of wine.

quotes.quote: Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
quotes.context: Asked by a dying criminal who rebuked the one next to him.

quotes.quote: Be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image.
quotes.context: A flat refusal delivered on the plain of Dura.

quotes.quote: O king, live for ever. My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths.
quotes.context: Called up from a sealed den at first light.

quotes.quote: Rend your heart, and not your garments.
quotes.context: A prophet's call to repentance during a locust plague.

quotes.quote: Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips.
quotes.context: Said on seeing the Lord high and lifted up in the temple.

quotes.quote: Can these bones live?
quotes.context: A question put to a prophet standing in a valley of dry bones.

quotes.quote: What mean ye by this service?
quotes.context: The question the Passover meal was designed to provoke.

quotes.quote: Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh?
quotes.context: Said at a burning bush, the first of several excuses.

quotes.quote: These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
quotes.context: Announced about a calf he had just made from melted earrings.

quotes.quote: Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.
quotes.context: The minority report after forty days of spying out Canaan.

quotes.quote: Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice.
quotes.context: Said to a king who blamed the people for sparing the best sheep.

quotes.quote: The Lord forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the Lord's anointed.
quotes.context: Said in a cave, after cutting only the hem of a sleeping king's robe.

quotes.quote: Thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.
quotes.context: Part of a lament for a fallen friend and his father.

quotes.quote: Vanity of vanities; all is vanity.
quotes.context: The opening verdict of a book about life under the sun.

quotes.quote: Ye are the salt of the earth.
quotes.context: Said on a mountainside early in the Sermon on the Mount.

quotes.quote: Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.
quotes.context: Prayed while being nailed to a cross.

quotes.quote: Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God.
quotes.context: Answering a rich young ruler who ran up and knelt down.

quotes.quote: Woman, where are those thine accusers? hath no man condemned thee?
quotes.context: Asked after writing on the ground and watching a crowd walk away.

quotes.quote: Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?
quotes.context: An apostle who thought seven was already generous.

quotes.quote: Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
quotes.context: Said at the knees of Jesus after a net-breaking catch of fish.

quotes.quote: To me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
quotes.context: Written to the Philippians while in chains.

quotes.quote: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
quotes.context: Written about learning contentment in plenty and in want.

quotes.quote: Shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.
quotes.context: A request made in the upper room on the last night.

quotes.quote: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
quotes.answer: The father of the demon-possessed boy
accept: the father of the demon possessed boy
quotes.context: Cried out with tears by a desperate parent at the foot of a mountain.

quotes.quote: What is this that thou hast done? The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.
quotes.context: An explanation offered in a garden, deflecting blame.

quotes.quote: The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.
quotes.context: The first recorded excuse in human history.
